title: Why washing hands works
examples: What kind of germs are on my hands?
Is washing hands enough to stop sickness?
How long should I really wash my hands for?

explain.say: Some tiny things called germs can live on your hands.
Soap has special bits that grab onto these germs.
When you wash, the soap traps the germs in little bubbles.
You must scrub for about twenty seconds to wash well.
Washing hands stops germs from moving to others.
When you are done, dry your hands with a clean towel.

draw.text: Dry hands with a clean towel

faq.q: Do I need soap if I just rinse with water?
faq.a: No, soap is important because it helps lift the germs off your skin. You can also ask, 'Is water enough to clean germs?' or 'Do I need soap to wash my hands?'
asks: Is water enough to clean germs?
Do I need soap to wash my hands?

faq.q: How long is twenty seconds exactly?
faq.a: Twenty seconds is about the time it takes to sing the 'Happy Birthday' song twice. You might also ask, 'What does twenty seconds feel like?' or 'How long should I scrub?'
asks: What does twenty seconds feel like?

faq.q: Can germs live on my hands forever?
faq.a: Germs can survive on surfaces for a while, but washing with soap removes most of them. You could also ask, 'Are germs permanent?' or 'How long do germs last on things?'
asks: How long do germs last on things?

faq.q: What if I wash my hands but still get sick?
faq.a: Sometimes you can still get sick because germs can enter through other ways besides your hands. You might ask, 'Can I still get sick?' or 'Does washing hands stop everything?'

faq.q: Should I wash my hands before eating?
faq.a: Yes, washing your hands before eating is very important for good health. You could also ask, 'When should I wash my hands?' or 'Is it good to wash hands before food?'
asks: When should I wash my hands?
Is it good to wash hands before food?

facts: Soap molecules have parts that can grab onto germs.
Washing hands for twenty seconds helps remove germs.
Germs can spread from hands to other people or objects.
Drying hands with a clean towel is the final step.

quiz.say: Soap helps clean germs because it:
quiz.why: The soap molecules surround the germs, trapping them so they can be washed away.

wrong.0: While soap can smell nice, its main job is cleaning, not just smelling good.
wrong.2: Soap does not kill all germs, but it traps them so they wash away.
wrong.3: Soap is not a harsh chemical that burns germs off your skin.

quiz.say: To wash hands properly, you should scrub for a time equal to:
quiz.why: This duration gives you enough time to scrub all parts of your hands thoroughly.

wrong.1: Rinsing alone is not enough time to scrub the soap onto the germs.
wrong.2: You must scrub the backs of your hands and between your fingers too.
wrong.3: Five seconds is too short a time to wash away all the tiny germs.

quiz.say: If you touch a doorknob after washing, you are:
quiz.why: Touching a surface after washing means you can pick up new germs from that surface.

wrong.1: Touching a surface means you are picking up whatever is already there.
wrong.2: Touching a surface does not make the germs vanish; it just moves them.
wrong.3: While it shows you are touching things, it also shows germs can stick to surfaces.
